title: Personal Credit Cards: whether an active checking account limits the points applied to the card balance
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: points applied to the card balance, by checking account status

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line and reads the cardholder's checking accounts. When a cardholder uses rewards points to pay down a card's balance through a statement credit on that card, it decides how many points the statement credit uses.

## Rule

1. When the cardholder holds a PCB checking account whose status is active, which can receive any points beyond the balance later, the statement credit uses the lesser of the card's unredeemed points and the points that cover the balance, so the card is not pushed into a credit balance.
2. When the cardholder holds no active PCB checking account, all unredeemed points are applied.

Any PCB checking account of the cardholder in active status satisfies the first branch; it need not be the card's autopay source. The status is read from the bank's checking account records.

## Branch table

| Cardholder holds an active PCB checking account | Points applied |
|---|---|
| yes | the lesser of the unredeemed points and the points that cover the balance |
| no | all unredeemed points |

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

| Unredeemed points | Points that cover the balance | Active checking account | Points applied |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25000 | 7180 | yes | 7180 |
| 25000 | 7180 | no | 25000, and the card moves into a credit balance |
| 5000 | 7180 | yes | 5000 |
| 5000 | 7180 | no | 5000 |

## Wrong reading and correct basis

- **Wrong:** always apply all points. **Correct:** with an active checking account, apply only up to the points that cover the balance.
- **Wrong:** the checking account must be the autopay source. **Correct:** any active PCB checking account of the cardholder counts.
